lessons.title: 1.1 Introduce Yourself and Others
lessons.notes_html:
About This Lesson

This is a speaking lesson. You talk in class and introduce yourself and your friends. There are no written questions in this lesson, so practise speaking with your partner.

What to Say

  • Say your name: "My name is ..."
  • Say your age: "I am ... years old."
  • Say your class: "I am in class three."
  • Tell about your eyes and hair.
  • Tell what you like and do not like.

A Model Introduction

In the Writing lesson of this unit, Ali introduces himself like this: "My name is Ali. I am eight years old. I am in class three. My eyes are brown and my hair is black. I like reading books and playing football. I do not like fighting and telling lies."

Key Points

  • We introduce ourselves by telling our name, age and class.
  • We can also tell about our eyes, hair and the things we like.
  • Speak clearly and politely when you introduce yourself and others.

mcqs.why: In the model introduction, Ali's hair is black.

mcqs.why: Ali says, "I like reading books and playing football."

mcqs.why: Ali says, "I do not like fighting and telling lies."

mcqs.why: When we introduce ourselves or others, we tell the name first.

mcqs.q: How should we speak when we introduce ourselves?
mcqs.why: This is a speaking lesson, and we should speak clearly and politely when we introduce ourselves and others.

lessons.title: 1.2 The Treasure
lessons.notes_html:
The Story

An old farmer worked alone in his fields. He had five sons. The sons were young and strong but lazy and selfish. They fought with one another all the time.

What Happened

  • The farmer worked alone because he wanted his sons to go to school.
  • When he told his sons to work, they became angry because they did not want to work.
  • The farmer told them there was gold in the field, so they dug the field.
  • After digging, the farmer told them to sow some seeds in the field.
  • They had a good crop and sold it for a good price.
  • Then the sons decided to work hard.

Words to Learn

  • Farmer: a man who works in the fields and grows food for us.
  • Hard working: someone who works hard.
  • Selfish: caring about oneself.
  • Lazy: those who do not like to work.
  • Sow: to put seeds in the ground.
  • Secret: something you do not tell everybody.
  • Good price: lots of money.
  • Treasure: money, gold etc.

Key Points

  • The farmer was old and hard working.
  • His five sons were young, lazy and selfish.
  • Hard work is the real treasure.

options: A man who works in the fields
A man who flies a plane
A man who teaches in a school

mcqs.why: There are six people in the story: the old farmer and his five sons.

mcqs.why: The farmer was hard working. He worked alone in his fields for many years.

mcqs.q: Which words describe the farmer's sons?
mcqs.why: The sons were young, lazy and selfish. They fought with one another all the time.

mcqs.q: Why did the farmer work alone in the field?
options: He wanted his sons to go to school
mcqs.why: The farmer worked alone in the field because he wanted his sons to go to school.

mcqs.q: Why did the sons become angry when he told them to work?
options: They did not want to work
mcqs.why: When he told his sons to work, they became angry because they did not want to work.

mcqs.q: Why did the farmer tell his sons to dig the field?
options: Because there was gold in the field
mcqs.why: The farmer told his sons to dig the field because there was gold in the field.

mcqs.q: What did the farmer tell his sons to do after they had dug the field?
options: Sow some seeds in the field
mcqs.why: After they had dug the field, the farmer told them to sow some seeds in the field.

mcqs.q: What is the meaning of "sow"?
options: To put seeds in the ground
mcqs.why: In the story's word list, "sow" means to put seeds in the ground.

mcqs.q: What is the meaning of "treasure"?
mcqs.why: In the story's word list, "treasure" means money, gold etc.

lessons.title: 1.3 a Apostrophe 's
lessons.notes_html:
Nouns in the Picnic Text

A noun is the name of a person, place, animal or thing. In the text "Going for a Picnic", the nouns are: Salma, family, picnic, food, drinks, basket, father, breakfast, car, colour, skipping rope, Farid, football, camera, mother, purse, radio and farm.

Apostrophe 's

We use 's to show that something belongs to someone.

  • It is Farid's football.
  • It is mother's purse.
  • It is father's camera.
  • It is the family's car.
  • It is the family's radio.

Rewrite with 's

  • The trunk of an elephant: The elephant's trunk is long.
  • The roar of a lion: The lion's roar is loud.
  • The neck of a giraffe: The giraffe's neck is long.
  • The home of a bird: The bird's home is a nest.

Key Points

  • We use 's to show that something belongs to someone.
  • We write the owner's name first and then add 's.

mcqs.q: What does 's show in a sentence?
options: That a question is being asked
mcqs.why: We use 's to show that something belongs to someone, like Farid's football.

mcqs.q: In the picnic text, whose football is it?
mcqs.why: The answer in the book is: It is Farid's football.

mcqs.q: In the picnic text, whose purse is it?
mcqs.why: The answer in the book is: It is mother's purse.

mcqs.q: In the picnic text, whose camera is it?
mcqs.why: The answer in the book is: It is father's camera.

mcqs.q: In the picnic text, whose car is it?
mcqs.why: The answer in the book is: It is the family's car.

mcqs.q: Rewrite using 's: The trunk of an elephant is long.
mcqs.why: We put 's after the owner: The elephant's trunk is long.

mcqs.q: Rewrite using 's: The roar of a lion is loud.
mcqs.why: We put 's after the owner: The lion's roar is loud.

mcqs.q: Rewrite using 's: The neck of a giraffe is long.
mcqs.why: We put 's after the owner: The giraffe's neck is long.

mcqs.q: Rewrite using 's: The home of a bird is a nest.
options: The bird home's is a nest
The homes bird is a nest
The bird's home is a nest
The birds home is a nest
mcqs.why: We put 's after the owner: The bird's home is a nest.

mcqs.q: Which of these words is a noun in the picnic text?
mcqs.why: Basket is one of the nouns in the text "Going for a Picnic". The other words are not nouns from the text.

lessons.title: 1.3 b Pronouns and Possessive Pronouns
lessons.notes_html:
Pronouns and Their Possessive Forms

PronounPossessive Form
Imine
Youyours
Hehis
Shehers
Itits
Theytheirs

Note: For "she", the possessive pronoun is hers. We use "her" before a noun, like "her book".

Fill in the Blanks

  • It's your hat. It's yours.
  • It's my car. It's mine.
  • It's our house. It's ours.
  • They're his trousers. They're his.
  • It's their anniversary. It's theirs.
  • They're your CDs. They're yours.

The Wallet Dialogue

Amna, Ahmed and Javeria talk about a wallet. They use mine, yours and hers to tell whose wallet it is. At the end Javeria says, "Wallet is mine. Please give me."

Key Points

  • Possessive pronouns show that something belongs to someone.
  • I - mine, you - yours, he - his, she - hers, it - its, they - theirs.

mcqs.q: What is the possessive form of "I"?
mcqs.why: The possessive form of "I" is "mine", as in: It's my car. It's mine.

mcqs.q: What is the possessive form of "you"?
mcqs.why: The possessive form of "you" is "yours", as in: It's your hat. It's yours.

mcqs.q: What is the possessive form of "he"?
mcqs.why: The possessive form of "he" is "his", as in: They're his trousers. They're his.

mcqs.q: What is the possessive form of "she"?
mcqs.why: The possessive form of "she" is "hers". We use "her" before a noun, like her book.

mcqs.q: What is the possessive form of "it"?
mcqs.why: In the matching exercise of the book, the possessive form of "it" is "its".

mcqs.q: What is the possessive form of "they"?
mcqs.why: The possessive form of "they" is "theirs", as in: It's their anniversary. It's theirs.

mcqs.q: Complete the sentence: It's my car. It's _____.
mcqs.why: "My" goes with "mine": It's my car. It's mine.

mcqs.q: Complete the sentence: It's our house. It's _____.
mcqs.why: "Our" goes with "ours": It's our house. It's ours.

mcqs.q: Complete the sentence: It's their anniversary. It's _____.
mcqs.why: "Their" goes with "theirs": It's their anniversary. It's theirs.

mcqs.q: In the wallet dialogue, Javeria says, "Wallet is _____."
mcqs.why: Javeria says, "Oh! Wallet is mine. Please give me."

lessons.title: 1.4 Writing - About Myself
lessons.notes_html:
About Myself (Model)

  • I am eight years old.
  • I am in class three.
  • My eyes are brown and my hair is black.

Writing about a Friend

Model: "My friend Ahmed is eight years old. He is in class three. His eyes are black and his hair is black. He is kind and helpful. We read and play together every day."

Key Points

lessons.title: 2.1 Enquiring about Health
lessons.notes_html:
About This Lesson

This is a speaking lesson. You talk with a partner and ask about health. There are no written questions in this lesson, so practise speaking in class.

Asking about Health

  • We ask a friend: "How are you?"
  • A polite answer is: "I am fine, thank you."
  • When a friend is sick, we ask about his or her health and wish him or her well.

Health Words in This Unit

The reading lesson of this unit uses these words: sick, fever, stomach-ache (a pain in the stomach), doctor and medicine. The doctor tells Farah to take rest, drink lots of water and not to eat spicy food.

Key Points

  • We ask "How are you?" to enquire about someone's health.
  • We answer politely: "I am fine, thank you."

lessons.title: 2.2 Healthy Eating Habits
lessons.notes_html:
Before Reading

In the break time, we eat our food and play with our friends. We eat fruit and a sandwich. Our mother gives us simple and healthy food from home.

The Story

  • Farah and Salma go to the same school. They are classmates and good friends.
  • Salma is strong and healthy. She likes fresh fruits and vegetables and loves food cooked by her mother.
  • Farah is weak and thin. She likes burgers and spicy food.
  • Sometimes they share their food.
  • One day Farah ate a spicy bun kabab. She also had a glass of sherbet and an ice-candy.
  • Farah fell sick. She had a stomach-ache and fever, so she did not go to school.
  • The doctor gave her medicine. He told her to take rest, drink lots of water and not to eat spicy food.
  • Farah promised: "I will never eat food sold outside the school gate."

Words to Learn

  • Snack: a small meal eaten in a hurry.
  • Tasty: having a good taste.
  • Spicy: having lots of salt and chillies.
  • Simple food: not having too many spices.
  • Stomach-ache: a pain in the stomach.

Key Points

  • Simple and healthy food keeps us strong and healthy.
  • Too much spicy food can make us sick.
  • We should eat food from home and drink lots of water.

lessons.title: 2.3 Imperative Sentences
lessons.notes_html:
Imperative Sentences

Imperative sentences tell us to do something or not to do something. Parents and teachers often use them.

Things to Do

  • Wash hands before meals.
  • Eat fresh food.
  • Keep food covered.
  • Drink clean water.
  • Thank Allah after having meals.
  • Brush teeth after meals.

Things Not to Do

  • Do not waste food.
  • Do not eat between meals.
  • Do not play in dirty water.
  • Do not eat lots of sweets.
  • Do not throw rubbish on the road.

What Parents Tell Us

Parents tell us to do: wash your hands before meals, do your homework on time, go to bed early. Parents tell us not to: waste food, play in dirty water, eat too many sweets.

Key Points

  • Imperative sentences give an order, advice or a request.
  • "Do not" sentences tell us the things we should not do.

mcqs.why: Washing hands before meals is in the "things to do" list of the lesson.

lessons.title: 2.3 Using 'a' and 'an' - Singular and Plural Nouns
lessons.notes_html:
Using 'a' and 'an'

  • A potato has an eye, but it cannot see with it.
  • Jamil wanted an apple.
  • An elephant can eat a peanut, but it will still be hungry.
  • I saw an egg in the nest. A little bird came out of it.

We use an before words that begin with a vowel sound (a, e, i, o, u), and a before other words.

Singular and Plural Nouns

  • I had one glass of milk and two glasses of juice.
  • There were three boxes on the table, but one box fell down.
  • All the paint brushes are in one box.
  • All the peaches are sweet.
  • There is one patch on your shirt.

Key Points

  • Use "an" before a vowel sound and "a" before other sounds.
  • Singular means one; plural means more than one.

mcqs.q: _____ apple is on the table. (Choose the correct word)
mcqs.why: Apple begins with a vowel sound, so we use "an": Jamil wanted an apple.

mcqs.q: _____ potato has an eye. (Choose the correct word)
mcqs.why: Potato does not begin with a vowel sound, so we use "a": A potato has an eye.

mcqs.q: _____ elephant can eat a peanut. (Choose the correct word)
mcqs.why: Elephant begins with a vowel sound, so we use "an": An elephant can eat a peanut.

mcqs.q: An elephant can eat _____ peanut. (Choose the correct word)
mcqs.why: Peanut does not begin with a vowel sound, so we use "a": An elephant can eat a peanut.

mcqs.q: I saw _____ egg in the nest. (Choose the correct word)
mcqs.why: Egg begins with a vowel sound, so we use "an": I saw an egg in the nest.

mcqs.q: _____ little bird came out of it. (Choose the correct word)
mcqs.why: Bird does not begin with a vowel sound, so we use "a": A little bird came out of it.

mcqs.q: I had one glass of milk and two _____ of juice.
mcqs.why: Two means more than one, so we use the plural: two glasses of juice.

mcqs.q: There were three boxes on the table, but one _____ fell down.
mcqs.why: One means singular, so we use "box": one box fell down.

mcqs.q: All the _____ are sweet. (peach)
mcqs.why: "All" shows more than one, so we use the plural: All the peaches are sweet.

mcqs.q: There is one _____ on your shirt. (patch)
mcqs.why: "One" shows singular, so we use "patch": There is one patch on your shirt.

lessons.title: 2.4 Writing a Paragraph - Breakfast
lessons.notes_html:
Parts of a Paragraph

A paragraph has a title, a topic sentence, detail sentences and a closing sentence.

The paragraph "Breakfast" is about breakfast. Its topic sentence is: "Having breakfast is good for health."

The Mind Map

The mind map words about breakfast are: spicy, kebab, paratha, rice, juice, butter, boiled egg, milk/tea/lassi, and "parents make". The words "after school" do NOT tell about breakfast, so we put a cross on them.

Model Paragraph

"Breakfast. Having breakfast is good for health. My mother makes breakfast for me. I eat a paratha and a boiled egg. I drink a glass of milk. A good breakfast keeps me happy and active in school."

Key Points

  • The topic sentence tells what the paragraph is about.
  • Detail sentences give more information about the topic.
  • The closing sentence ends the paragraph.

mcqs.why: The paragraph is about breakfast. Its topic sentence is: Having breakfast is good for health.

lessons.title: 3.1 Waiting for School Bus
lessons.notes_html:
About This Lesson

This is a speaking lesson. You talk in class about waiting for the school bus. There are no written questions in this lesson, so practise speaking with your partner.

Stay Safe while Waiting

The reading lessons of this unit teach us how to stay safe on the road:

  • Wait for the bus at a safe place, on the footpath.
  • Before you cross the road, look left and right.
  • Remember the traffic lights: red means stop, yellow means get ready or wait, and green means go.
  • Never run after a ball on the road. A fast car can hit you.
  • Always remember the motto: SAFETY FIRST.

Key Points

  • We wait for the school bus at a safe place and stay careful on the road.
  • Looking left and right before crossing keeps us safe.

lessons.title: 3.2 Safety Measures - Traffic Lights
lessons.notes_html:
Traffic Lights

  • The traffic lights are red, yellow (amber) and green.
  • We see them on roads, at crossings and near traffic signals in the city.
  • Red means stop.
  • Yellow means get ready or wait.
  • Green means go.

The Picture

A boy is holding a little girl to keep her safe on the road. Her ball has fallen on the road. If the boy does not hold her, she can run after the ball on the road. A fast car can hit her and she can get hurt.

Key Points

  • Red means stop, yellow means get ready or wait, and green means go.
  • We must never run onto the road after a ball.

mcqs.q: What colours are the traffic lights?
mcqs.why: The traffic lights are red, yellow (amber) and green.

mcqs.q: What does red mean?
mcqs.why: Red means stop, yellow means get ready or wait, and green means go.

mcqs.q: What does yellow mean?
mcqs.why: The lesson says: Yellow means get ready or wait. Red means stop and green means go.

lessons.title: 3.4 Plurals, Proper Nouns and Countable Nouns
lessons.notes_html:
Plural Nouns

  • person - people
  • man - men
  • woman - women
  • child - children
  • foot - feet
  • goose - geese

3 uncles + 7 fathers = 10 men. 5 grandmothers + 7 mothers = 12 women. 1 white goose + 2 brown geese = 3 geese.

Proper Nouns

Proper nouns are names of particular people, places or things. They begin with a capital letter. In the lesson they are: Karachi, Queens Road, Safari Park, Kiamari and Jan Mohammad Jamali Primary School.

Festivals and days are also proper nouns: Hindus have a holiday called Divali. It is celebrated in November. The last Friday of Ramzan is called Juma-tul-Wida.

Countable and Uncountable Nouns

  • Countable nouns: books, glass, pencils, bags, bottles, songs, desk. We can count them, like one book, two books.
  • Uncountable nouns: ice, milk, music, wood. We cannot count them; we measure them.

Key Points

  • Some plurals change the whole word: child - children, foot - feet.
  • Proper nouns begin with a capital letter.

Note: The contents page of the textbook prints this lesson as "Writing a Degree". That is a misprint. The lesson is about writing the steps of making a kabab roll.

lessons.title: 5.2 Rashid Minhas Shaheed, Nishan-e-Haider
lessons.notes_html:
Before Reading

A pilot flies an aeroplane. We can fly a kite, but only a pilot can fly an aeroplane. Rashid Minhas Shaheed is a famous pilot of Pakistan. He was a brave pilot of the Pakistan Air Force.

His Life

  • Rashid Minhas was born in Karachi on 17th February, 1951.
  • When he was a little boy, he read stories about flying aeroplanes.
  • His hobby was collecting different kinds of model aeroplanes.
  • He joined the Pakistan Air Force and became a GD pilot.
  • On 20th August, 1971, he was about to take off in a T-33 plane for his second solo flight. His instructor hijacked the plane. Rashid fought bravely, the plane crashed, and he gave his life for his country.
  • He was awarded the Nishan-e-Haider for his bravery and sacrifice.

How He Was Honoured

  • The airforce base at Kamra was renamed PAF Base Minhas after him.
  • Rashid Minhas Road at Karachi is named after him.
  • In December 2003, Pakistan Post printed a two-rupee postage stamp with his picture on it.

Words to Learn

  • Hobby: favourite pastime.
  • Solo: alone.
  • Hijacked: taken away by force.
  • Award: an honour.
  • Take off: plane leaves the ground.
  • Renamed: changed the name.

The first person to get the Nishan-e-Haider was Captain Muhammad Sarwar Shaheed.

Key Points

  • Rashid Minhas loved aeroplanes from his childhood.
  • He gave his life for his country on 20th August, 1971.

lessons.title: 5.4 Writing a Story

The Outline

Village boy wearing a red shirt - hears a loud bang - train track blown up - hears a train in the distance - runs toward the train and waves his shirt - train stops - saved!

lessons.title: 6.3 a Use of Was and Were
lessons.notes_html:
About This Lesson

This page introduces was and were. The written practice for this lesson is in the next lesson, "Simple Past Tense - Was, Were".

The Rule

  • We use was with I, he, she, it and one person or thing.
  • We use were with you, we, they and more than one person or thing.
  • Was and were tell about the past.

Examples from the Next Lesson

  • I was at the zoo last Saturday.
  • Beena and Bilal were with me.
  • Sana was not with us.

Key Points

  • Was is for one; were is for more than one, and for "you".
  • Was and were are past tense words.

mcqs.q: I _____ at the zoo last Saturday.
mcqs.why: With "I" we use "was": I was at the zoo last Saturday.

mcqs.q: Beena and Bilal _____ with me.
mcqs.why: Beena and Bilal are two people, so we use "were": Beena and Bilal were with me.

mcqs.q: Sana _____ not with us.
mcqs.why: Sana is one person, so we use "was": Sana was not with us.

mcqs.q: _____ Sana at the park on Saturday?
mcqs.why: Sana is one person, so the question begins with "Was": Was Sana at the park on Saturday?

mcqs.q: _____ there many people at the zoo?
mcqs.why: Many people means more than one, so we use "Were": Were there many people at the zoo?

mcqs.q: _____ you tired in the evening?
mcqs.why: With "you" we use "were": Were you tired in the evening?

mcqs.q: "Was" is used with _____.
mcqs.why: We use "was" with I, he, she and it. With you, we and they, we use "were".

mcqs.q: "Were" is used with _____.
mcqs.why: We use "were" with you, we and they. With he, she and it, we use "was".

mcqs.q: She _____ at home yesterday.
mcqs.why: She is one person and the sentence is about the past, so we use "was".

mcqs.q: They _____ happy at the zoo.
mcqs.why: "They" takes "were": They were happy at the zoo.

lessons.title: 6.3 Verbs that Tell about the Past
lessons.notes_html:
Present and Past

  • laugh - laughed
  • scare - scared
  • play - played
  • finish - finished

The kittens finished all the milk. They played with a balloon. The balloon burst and it scared the kittens. It was funny, we all laughed.

Note: The contents page of the textbook prints "Regular/Irregular Nouns" for this part of Unit 6. That is a misprint. The lesson is about verbs that tell about the past.

Making the Past Tense

  • Add d: dance - danced, bathe - bathed, struggle - struggled, paste - pasted, blame - blamed.
  • Add ed: intend - intended, detect - detected, scold - scolded, roar - roared.
  • convey - conveyed.

More Pairs from the Reading

plan - planned, purchase - purchased, look - looked, pay - paid, count - counted, do - did, play - played, finish - finished, laugh - laughed, go - went.

Answering in the Past

"I drank a glass of water at lunch time. I went shopping yesterday. When Sara opened the parrot's cage, the parrot flew away. I left for school at 7.30 in the morning. The school bell rang at 8 o'clock."

Key Points

  • Most verbs make the past tense with d or ed.
  • Some verbs change in a special way: go - went, do - did, pay - paid.

mcqs.q: What is the past tense of "laugh"?
mcqs.why: Laugh - laughed. It was funny, we all laughed.

mcqs.q: What is the past tense of "play"?
mcqs.why: Play - played. They played with a balloon.

mcqs.q: What is the past tense of "dance"?
mcqs.why: Dance ends with e, so we add only d: dance - danced.

mcqs.q: What is the past tense of "pay"?
mcqs.why: Pay changes in a special way: pay - paid.

mcqs.q: What is the past tense of "do"?
mcqs.why: Do changes in a special way in the past tense: do - did, like go - went.

mcqs.q: What is the past tense of "go"?
mcqs.why: Go changes in a special way: go - went, as in: I went shopping yesterday.

mcqs.q: The kittens _____ all the milk.
mcqs.why: The solved sentence is: The kittens finished all the milk.

mcqs.q: The balloon burst and it _____ the kittens.
mcqs.why: The solved sentence is: The balloon burst and it scared the kittens.

mcqs.q: When Sara opened the parrot's cage, the parrot _____ away.
mcqs.why: The model answer says: When Sara opened the parrot's cage, the parrot flew away.

mcqs.q: The school bell _____ at 8 o'clock.
mcqs.why: The model answer says: The school bell rang at 8 o'clock.

lessons.title: 6.4 Writing a Letter of Invitation
lessons.notes_html:
Sana's Letter

  • Sana wrote this letter of invitation.
  • She wrote it from House No. 25, High Street, Karachi, on 5th August, 2014.
  • She invited Sara to an Eid Party at her house.
  • The party is on 10th August.
  • It will start at 4 o'clock and end at 6 o'clock.

A Model Letter

Fatima writes from House No. 10, Main Street, Karachi, on 1st October: "Dear Salma, Please come to my Birthday Party at my house on 5th October. It will be from 5 o'clock to 7 o'clock. I will be very happy if you can come. Your friend, Fatima."

Key Points

  • A letter of invitation tells the date, time and place of the party.
  • We write our address and the date at the top of the letter.

mcqs.why: It will start at 4 o'clock and end at 6 o'clock.

mcqs.why: It will end at 6 o'clock. It will be from 4 o'clock to 6 o'clock.

mcqs.q: In the model letter, Fatima invites Salma to a _____ party.
mcqs.why: Fatima writes: Please come to my Birthday Party at my house on 5th October.

mcqs.q: Fatima's party will be from 5 o'clock to _____ o'clock.
mcqs.why: The model letter says: It will be from 5 o'clock to 7 o'clock.

mcqs.q: A letter of invitation must tell the date, time and _____ of the party.
mcqs.why: Sana's letter tells Sara the place (her house), the date (10th August) and the time (4 to 6 o'clock).

lessons.title: 6.5 Poem - The School Room Clock
lessons.notes_html:
About the Poem

This is a poem about the clock in our school room. Read the poem aloud in class. There are no written questions for this poem in the book.

Clock Facts from This Unit

  • A clock has a face and two hands, and it tells the time.
  • The small hand tells hours.
  • The big hand tells minutes.
  • The thin hand ticks seconds.
  • At half past three, the big hand is on 6.

Key Points

  • The school room clock tells us the time of our lessons.
  • We should reach school on time.

mcqs.q: The poem "The School Room Clock" is about a _____.

mcqs.q: The big hand of a clock tells _____.

mcqs.q: A clock has a _____ and two hands.
mcqs.why: The riddle in this unit asks: What has a face, two hands, and tells the time? A clock.

mcqs.q: At five o'clock, the small hand is on _____.

mcqs.q: At half past three, the big hand is on _____.
mcqs.why: At half past three, the small hand is just past 3 and the big hand is on 6.

mcqs.q: We should reach school _____.
mcqs.why: In this unit's model answers we read: I left for school at 7.30 in the morning. I reached school on time.

lessons.title: Three in a Row - Word Families
lessons.notes_html:
How to Play

In each puzzle, find three words of the same family. Draw a line through the three words.

The Four Puzzles

  • Puzzle 1: mango, apple, banana - they are all fruits.
  • Puzzle 2: yellow, blue, red - they are all colours.
  • Puzzle 3: arm, leg, foot - they are all parts of the body.
  • Puzzle 4: spring, winter, summer - they are all seasons.

Key Points

  • Words of one family tell about the same kind of things.
  • Fruits, colours, body parts and seasons are four word families in this game.

mcqs.q: In Puzzle 1, which three words are of the same family?
mcqs.why: The three words of the same family in Puzzle 1 are mango, apple and banana.

mcqs.q: The words in Puzzle 1 are names of _____.
mcqs.why: The words mango, apple and banana are names of fruits.

mcqs.q: In Puzzle 2, which three words are of the same family?
mcqs.why: The three words of the same family in Puzzle 2 are yellow, blue and red.

mcqs.q: The words in Puzzle 2 are names of _____.
mcqs.why: The words yellow, blue and red are names of colours.

mcqs.q: In Puzzle 3, which three words are of the same family?
mcqs.why: The three words of the same family in Puzzle 3 are arm, leg and foot.

mcqs.q: The words in Puzzle 3 are names of _____.
mcqs.why: The words arm, leg and foot are names of body parts.

mcqs.q: In Puzzle 4, which three words are of the same family?
mcqs.why: The three words of the same family in Puzzle 4 are spring, winter and summer.

mcqs.q: The words in Puzzle 4 are names of _____.
mcqs.why: The words spring, winter and summer are names of seasons.

mcqs.q: Which of these words is a fruit?
mcqs.why: In Puzzle 1, banana is a fruit, like mango and apple. Carrot, chips and juice are not fruits.

mcqs.q: Which of these words is a season?
mcqs.why: In Puzzle 4, winter is a season, like spring and summer.
